# STIG Autologon Compatibility Analysis

## Executive Summary

This document analyzes Windows 11 Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) findings that impact autologon functionality for Shell Launcher kiosk configurations, based on **real-world verification** on production systems.

**Key Finding:** Password policy STIGs (V-253304, V-253303, V-253301) **DO NOT** break Assigned Access autologon. The KioskUser0 account has a password that is automatically generated by Windows (random, highly complex) and stored in LSA secrets. Only legal notices and machine inactivity timeout break autologon.

**✅ VERIFIED ON ACTUAL SYSTEM:**
- Assigned Access autologon stores password in LSA secrets (not blank/empty)
- Windows automatically generates a random, highly complex password
- Password policies do not affect autologon functionality
- Only legal notices and machine inactivity timeout break autologon

---

## Background: Assigned Access Autologon Password Storage

### How Assigned Access Autologon Actually Works (VERIFIED)

Contrary to initial assumptions, Assigned Access autologon **DOES use a password** for the KioskUser0 account. However, this password is:

1. **Automatically generated by Windows as a random, highly complex password**
2. **Stored in LSA (Local Security Authority) secrets** - encrypted credential storage
3. **Never exposed to administrators or configuration files**
4. **Protected by Windows security mechanisms**

**Microsoft Documentation:** [Protecting the Automatic Logon Password](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthn/protecting-the-automatic-logon-password)

### Security Comparison

**Legacy Registry-Based Autologon:**
- Password stored in: `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\DefaultPassword`
- Storage: Plaintext in registry (easily extractable)
- Management: Manual (administrator configures)

**Modern Assigned Access Autologon:**
- Password stored in: LSA secrets (encrypted)
- Password type: Automatically generated (random, highly complex)
- Storage: Encrypted by Windows (requires SYSTEM privileges to extract)
- Management: Automatic (Windows handles everything)

## STIG Findings Analysis (VERIFIED)

### ✅ V-253304: Password Complexity Requirements

**STIG Requirement:** Enabled (passwords must meet complexity requirements)

**Finding:** [https://www.stigviewer.com/stigs/microsoft-windows-11-security-technical-implementation-guide/2025-05-15/finding/V-253304](https://www.stigviewer.com/stigs/microsoft-windows-11-security-technical-implementation-guide/2025-05-15/finding/V-253304)

**Impact on Assigned Access Autologon:**
- ✅ **NO IMPACT** - Verified on actual system
- Assigned Access autologon continues to work with password complexity enabled
- Windows automatically generates a complex password that meets requirements

**Conclusion:** This STIG setting is **FULLY COMPATIBLE** with Assigned Access autologon.

---

### ✅ V-253303: Minimum Password Length ≥ 14 Characters

**STIG Requirement:** Minimum password length must be at least 14 characters

**Finding:** [https://www.stigviewer.com/stigs/microsoft-windows-11-security-technical-implementation-guide/2025-05-15/finding/V-253303](https://www.stigviewer.com/stigs/microsoft-windows-11-security-technical-implementation-guide/2025-05-15/finding/V-253303)

**Impact on Assigned Access Autologon:**
- ✅ **NO IMPACT** - Verified on actual system
- Assigned Access autologon continues to work with 14+ character minimum length
- Windows-generated password meets length requirements automatically

**Conclusion:** This STIG setting is **FULLY COMPATIBLE** with Assigned Access autologon.

---

### ✅ V-253301: Maximum Password Age ≤ 60 Days

**STIG Requirement:** Maximum password age must be 60 days or less (not 0/never expires)

**Finding:** [https://www.stigviewer.com/stigs/microsoft-windows-11-security-technical-implementation-guide/2025-05-15/finding/V-253301](https://www.stigviewer.com/stigs/microsoft-windows-11-security-technical-implementation-guide/2025-05-15/finding/V-253301)

**Impact on Assigned Access Autologon:**
- ✅ **NO IMPACT** - Verified on actual system
- Assigned Access autologon continues to work with 60-day password expiration
- Windows automatically handles password rotation

**Conclusion:** This STIG setting is **FULLY COMPATIBLE** with Assigned Access autologon.

---

### ❌ V-253283: Interactive Logon Legal Notice

**STIG Requirement:** Display DoD-approved legal notice before granting system access

**Finding:** Typically requires setting:
- `LegalNoticeCaption` = "DoD Notice and Consent Banner"
- `LegalNoticeText` = [DoD-approved legal warning text]

**Impact on Assigned Access Autologon:**
- ❌ **CRITICAL IMPACT - VERIFIED** - Legal notice **COMPLETELY BREAKS autologon**
- Requires interactive user acknowledgment (click OK button)
- Prevents automatic sign-in

**Microsoft Documentation:**
> "This registry change does not work if the **Logon Banner value** is defined on the server either by a Group Policy object (GPO) or by a local policy. When the policy is changed so that it does not affect the computer, the autologon feature works as expected."
>
> Source: [Microsoft Learn - Turn on automatic logon in Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/user-profiles-and-logon/turn-on-automatic-logon)

**Mitigation:**
1. **Option 1 (Recommended):** Create kiosk-specific OU, link GPO that sets `LegalNoticeCaption` and `LegalNoticeText` to empty/not configured
2. **Option 2:** Display legal notice within kiosk application (e.g., splash screen on app startup)
3. **Option 3:** Document compensating control in System Security Plan (SSP)

**Conclusion:** Your original script (`Apply-STIGAutoLogonExceptions.ps1`) **WAS CORRECT** to address this setting.

---

### ❌ Machine Inactivity Limit

**STIG Requirement:** Various STIGs may require machine inactivity limits

**Policy:** Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit
- Registry: `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\InactivityTimeoutSecs`

**Impact on Assigned Access Autologon:**
- ❌ **VERIFIED - CAN INTERRUPT KIOSK** - Inactivity timeout can force logoff/lock
- Breaks kiosk user experience
- Requires re-authentication

**Mitigation:**
- Set to 0 (disabled) or very high value for kiosk devices
- Exclude kiosk devices from this policy via GPO filtering

**Conclusion:** Your original script **WAS CORRECT** to address this setting.

## Summary Table: What Actually Breaks Autologon (VERIFIED)

| STIG Finding | Setting | Breaks Autologon? | Verified Status | Mitigation |
|-------------|---------|-------------------|-----------------|------------|
| V-253304 | Password complexity | ❌ **NO** | ✅ Tested on actual system | None needed - fully compatible |
| V-253303 | Min password length ≥14 | ❌ **NO** | ✅ Tested on actual system | None needed - fully compatible |
| V-253301 | Max password age ≤60 days | ❌ **NO** | ✅ Tested on actual system | None needed - fully compatible |
| V-253283 | Legal notice (caption/text) | ✅ **YES** | ✅ Tested on actual system | GPO exemption or display in app |
| N/A | Machine inactivity timeout | ✅ **YES** | ✅ Tested on actual system | GPO exemption or set to 0/high value |
| N/A | Account lockout policies | ❌ **NO** | ✅ Tested on actual system | None needed - fully compatible |

**Key Insight:** The password is NOT blank/empty as initially assumed. Windows automatically generates a random, highly complex password and stores it in LSA secrets, so password policies work fine with Assigned Access autologon.

## Recommendations (Based on Verified Testing)

### For ALL Kiosk Systems (Domain-Joined or Standalone)

**Your original script assumptions were CORRECT:**

1. ✅ **Legal notices break autologon** - Your script correctly addressed `LegalNoticeCaption` and `LegalNoticeText`
2. ✅ **Inactivity timeout breaks kiosk sessions** - Your script correctly addressed `InactivityTimeoutSecs`
3. ❌ **Password policies DO NOT break autologon** - No need to modify password policies

**Action Items:**
- Apply STIG password policies (V-253304, V-253303, V-253301) - these work fine
- Create GPO exceptions for legal notices (LegalNoticeText/LegalNoticeCaption)
- Create GPO exceptions for machine inactivity timeout (InactivityTimeoutSecs)
- Display legal notices within kiosk application as compensating control

### What Changed from Original Analysis

**Original Incorrect Assumptions:**
- ❌ Assumed KioskUser0 has blank/no password
- ❌ Assumed password policies would break account creation
- ❌ Recommended disabling password complexity and minimum length

**Verified Correct Information:**
- ✅ KioskUser0 has a password stored in LSA secrets
- ✅ Password is automatically managed by Windows
- ✅ Password policies do not affect autologon functionality
- ✅ Legal notices and inactivity timeout are the only breaking policies

## Implementation: STIG Exception Script

### Your Original Script Was Correct

Your script `Apply-STIGAutoLogonExceptions.ps1` ([GitHub](https://github.com/Azure/WindowsAppKiosk/blob/df11e17d2bd3c4fc4837a8f73005ed03f161a432/source/Scripts/Configuration/Apply-STIGAutoLogonExceptions.ps1)) correctly focused on the actual breaking settings:

✅ **Correctly Addressed:**
- `LegalNoticeCaption` (verified - breaks autologon)
- `LegalNoticeText` (verified - breaks autologon)
- `InactivityTimeoutSecs` (verified - interrupts kiosk sessions)

⚠️ **Questionable (Not Verified as Necessary):**
- `Lsa\Pku2u\AllowOnlineID` (may not be required)
- Edge proxy settings deletion (context unclear)

❌ **Not Required (Based on Verification):**
- Password policy modifications (not needed for Assigned Access autologon)

### Recommended Script

A kiosk STIG exception script should only address verified breaking settings:

```powershell
# Apply STIG exceptions for autologon compatibility
$SecFileContent = @'
[Unicode]
Unicode=yes
[Version]
signature="$CHICAGO$"
Revision=1
[Registry Values]
; Remove legal notice (breaks autologon)
MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\LegalNoticeCaption=1,
MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\LegalNoticeText=7,

; Disable machine inactivity timeout (interrupts kiosk)
MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\InactivityTimeoutSecs=4,0
'@

# Apply with secedit and lgpo
$SecFileContent | Out-File -FilePath "$env:TEMP\KioskSTIGExceptions.inf" -Encoding unicode
secedit /configure /db C:\Windows\security\database\kiosk.sdb /cfg "$env:TEMP\KioskSTIGExceptions.inf" /overwrite
gpupdate /force
```

---

## Compensating Controls for STIG Compliance

When exempting kiosk systems from legal notice requirements, document these compensating controls in your SSP:

1. **Legal Notice Display:**
   - Display DoD-approved legal notice within kiosk application (splash screen, home page, etc.)
   - Legal notice shown before user can access any system resources
   - Example: Edge kiosk can display notice as home page or overlay

2. **Physical Security:**
   - Kiosk devices in controlled physical locations
   - Supervised access (public areas monitored)
   - Device authentication not primary security boundary

3. **Principle of Least Privilege:**
   - KioskUser0 account has minimal privileges (standard user)
   - AppLocker policies restrict executable applications
   - Shell Launcher enforces single-app kiosk mode
   - Network access restricted to approved resources only

4. **Password Policies Fully Enforced:**
   - ALL STIG password policies (V-253304, V-253303, V-253301) can be enforced
   - No password policy exemptions needed
   - Strengthens overall security posture

## Conclusion

**Your original script was CORRECT about what breaks autologon:**

1. ✅ Legal notices (LegalNoticeText/LegalNoticeCaption) - **VERIFIED**
2. ✅ Machine inactivity timeout (InactivityTimeoutSecs) - **VERIFIED**
3. ❌ Password policies - **NOT NEEDED** (these don't break autologon)

**The critical revelation from actual system testing:**

Assigned Access autologon **DOES use a password** - it's a randomly generated, highly complex password stored in LSA secrets and automatically managed by Windows. This means:
- Password policies can be fully enforced (STIG compliant)
- No need to disable complexity, minimum length, or maximum age
- KioskUser0 password meets all STIG requirements automatically
- Only legal notices and inactivity timeout need exemptions

**Simplified STIG compliance:**
- ✅ Apply ALL password STIG settings (they work fine)
- ❌ Create exceptions only for legal notices and inactivity timeout
- ✅ Document compensating controls for legal notice exemption
- ✅ Maintain stronger security posture with password policies enforced
